audit_status.source_base: Greek Philippians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for rejoicing, peace beyond mind, worthy thought, contentment, partnership/gift, final greetings.

verses.restored: So then, my beloved and longed-for siblings, my joy and crown, stand firm thus in the Lord, beloved.

familiar.text: Therefore, my brethren dearly beloved and longed for, my joy and crown, so stand fast in the Lord, my dearly beloved.

modern.text: Therefore, my brothers, whom I love and long for, my joy and crown, that is how you must stand firm in the Lord, my beloved.

original.text: ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοὶ καὶ ἐπιπόθητοι, χαρὰ καὶ στέφανός μου, οὕτως στήκετε ἐν κυρίῳ, ἀγαπητοί.

verses.restored: I appeal to Euodia and I appeal to Syntyche to think the same in the Lord.

familiar.text: I beseech Euodias, and beseech Syntyche, that they be of the same mind in the Lord.

modern.text: I urge Euodia and Syntyche to agree with each other in the Lord.

original.text: Εὐοδίαν παρακαλῶ καὶ Συντύχην παρακαλῶ τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖν ἐν κυρίῳ.

verses.restored: Yes, I ask you also, true yokefellow, help these women, who struggled together with me in the good news, with Clement also and the rest of my coworkers, whose names are in book of life.

familiar.text: And I intreat thee also, true yokefellow, help those women which laboured with me in the gospel, with Clement also, and with other my fellowlabourers, whose names are in the book of life.

modern.text: Yes, and I ask you, my true yokefellow, to help these women who have labored with me for the gospel, along with Clement and the rest of my fellow workers, whose names are in the Book of Life.

original.text: ναὶ ἐρωτῶ καὶ σέ, ⸂γνήσιε σύζυγε⸃, συλλαμβάνου αὐταῖς, αἵτινες ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ συνήθλησάν μοι μετὰ καὶ Κλήμεντος καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν συνεργῶν μου, ὧν τὰ ὀνόματα ἐν βίβλῳ ζωῆς.

verses.restored: Rejoice in the Lord always; again I will say, rejoice.

familiar.text: Rejoice in the Lord alway: and again I say, Rejoice.

modern.text: Rejoice in the Lord always. I will say it again: Rejoice!

original.text: Χαίρετε ἐν κυρίῳ πάντοτε· πάλιν ἐρῶ, χαίρετε.

verses.restored: Let your gentleness/reasonableness be known to all humans. The Lord is near.

familiar.text: Let your moderation be known unto all men. The Lord is at hand.

modern.text: Let your gentleness be apparent to all. The Lord is near.

original.text: τὸ ἐπιεικὲς ὑμῶν γνωσθήτω πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις. ὁ κύριος ἐγγύς·

verses.restored: Be anxious about nothing, but in everything by prayer and petition with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to the Divine.

familiar.text: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.

modern.text: Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.

original.text: μηδὲν μεριμνᾶτε, ἀλλʼ ἐν παντὶ τῇ προσευχῇ καὶ τῇ δεήσει μετʼ εὐχαριστίας τὰ αἰτήματα ὑμῶν γνωριζέσθω πρὸς τὸν θεόν·

verses.restored: And the peace of the Divine, surpassing every mind, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Messiah Jesus.

familiar.text: And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.

modern.text: And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.

original.text: καὶ ἡ εἰρήνη τοῦ θεοῦ ἡ ὑπερέχουσα πάντα νοῦν φρουρήσει τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν καὶ τὰ νοήματα ὑμῶν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.

verses.restored: Finally, siblings, whatever is true, whatever honorable, whatever righteous/just, whatever pure, whatever lovely, whatever well-spoken, if any excellence and if any praise, calculate these things.

familiar.text: Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.

modern.text: Finally, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is admirable—if anything is excellent or praiseworthy—think on these things.

original.text: Τὸ λοιπόν, ἀδελφοί, ὅσα ἐστὶν ἀληθῆ, ὅσα σεμνά, ὅσα δίκαια, ὅσα ἁγνά, ὅσα προσφιλῆ, ὅσα εὔφημα, εἴ τις ἀρετὴ καὶ εἴ τις ἔπαινος, ταῦτα λογίζεσθε·

verses.restored: What you also learned and received and heard and saw in me, practice these things; and the Divine of peace will be with you.

familiar.text: Those things, which ye have both learned, and received, and heard, and seen in me, do: and the God of peace shall be with you.

modern.text: Whatever you have learned or received or heard from me, or seen in me, put it into practice. And the God of peace will be with you. The Generosity of the Philippians (2 Corinthians 8:1–15)

original.text: ἃ καὶ ἐμάθετε καὶ παρελάβετε καὶ ἠκούσατε καὶ εἴδετε ἐν ἐμοί, ταῦτα πράσσετε· καὶ ὁ θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης ἔσται μεθʼ ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: But I rejoiced in the Lord greatly that now at last you revived thinking on my behalf; indeed you were thinking, but lacked opportunity.

familiar.text: But I rejoiced in the Lord greatly, that now at the last your care of me hath flourished again; wherein ye were also careful, but ye lacked opportunity.

modern.text: Now I rejoice greatly in the Lord that at last you have revived your concern for me. You were indeed concerned, but you had no opportunity to show it.

original.text: Ἐχάρην δὲ ἐν κυρίῳ μεγάλως ὅτι ἤδη ποτὲ ἀνεθάλετε τὸ ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ φρονεῖν, ἐφʼ ᾧ καὶ ἐφρονεῖτε ἠκαιρεῖσθε δέ.

verses.restored: Not that I speak according to lack, for I learned to be self-sufficient/content in whatever I am.

familiar.text: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.

modern.text: I am not saying this out of need, for I have learned to be content regardless of my circumstances.

original.text: οὐχ ὅτι καθʼ ὑστέρησιν λέγω, ἐγὼ γὰρ ἔμαθον ἐν οἷς εἰμι αὐτάρκης εἶναι·

verses.restored: I know how to be humbled, and I know how to abound; in each and every thing I have been initiated, both to be filled and to hunger, both to abound and to lack.

familiar.text: I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need.

modern.text: I know how to live humbly, and I know how to abound. I am accustomed to any and every situation—to being filled and being hungry, to having plenty and having need.

original.text: οἶδα καὶ ταπεινοῦσθαι, οἶδα καὶ περισσεύειν· ἐν παντὶ καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν μεμύημαι, καὶ χορτάζεσθαι καὶ πεινᾶν, καὶ περισσεύειν καὶ ὑστερεῖσθαι·

verses.restored: I have strength for all things in the One empowering me.

familiar.text: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.

modern.text: I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength.

original.text: πάντα ἰσχύω ἐν τῷ ἐνδυναμοῦντί ⸀με.

verses.restored: Nevertheless, you did beautifully/well sharing together with my pressure.

familiar.text: Notwithstanding ye have well done, that ye did communicate with my affliction.

modern.text: Nevertheless, you have done well to share in my affliction.

original.text: πλὴν καλῶς ἐποιήσατε συγκοινωνήσαντές μου τῇ θλίψει.

verses.restored: And you Philippians also know that in the beginning of the good news, when I went out from Macedonia, no assembly partnered with me in account of giving and receiving except you only,

familiar.text: Now ye Philippians know also, that in the beginning of the gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no church communicated with me as concerning giving and receiving, but ye only.

modern.text: And as you Philippians know, in the early days of the gospel, when I left Macedonia, no church but you partnered with me in the matter of giving and receiving.

original.text: Οἴδατε δὲ καὶ ὑμεῖς, Φιλιππήσιοι, ὅτι ἐν ἀρχῇ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, ὅτε ἐξῆλθον ἀπὸ Μακεδονίας, οὐδεμία μοι ἐκκλησία ἐκοινώνησεν εἰς λόγον δόσεως καὶ λήμψεως εἰ μὴ ὑμεῖς μόνοι,

verses.restored: because even in Thessalonica, more than once you sent into my need.

familiar.text: For even in Thessalonica ye sent once and again unto my necessity.

modern.text: For even while I was in Thessalonica, you provided for my needs again and again.

original.text: ὅτι καὶ ἐν Θεσσαλονίκῃ καὶ ἅπαξ καὶ δὶς εἰς τὴν χρείαν μοι ἐπέμψατε.

verses.restored: Not that I seek the gift, but I seek the fruit increasing into your account.

familiar.text: Not because I desire a gift: but I desire fruit that may abound to your account.

modern.text: Not that I am seeking a gift, but I am looking for the fruit that may be credited to your account.

original.text: οὐχ ὅτι ἐπιζητῶ τὸ δόμα, ἀλλὰ ἐπιζητῶ τὸν καρπὸν τὸν πλεονάζοντα εἰς λόγον ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: But I have received all and abound; I have been filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things from you, a fragrant aroma, acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to the Divine.

familiar.text: But I have all, and abound: I am full, having received of Epaphroditus the things which were sent from you, an odour of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, wellpleasing to God.

modern.text: I have all I need and more, now that I have received your gifts from Epaphroditus. They are a fragrant offering, an acceptable sacrifice, well-pleasing to God.

original.text: ἀπέχω δὲ πάντα καὶ περισσεύω· πεπλήρωμαι δεξάμενος παρὰ Ἐπαφροδίτου τὰ παρʼ ὑμῶν, ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας, θυσίαν δεκτήν, εὐάρεστον τῷ θεῷ.

verses.restored: And my Divine will fill every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Messiah Jesus.

familiar.text: But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.

modern.text: And my God will supply all your needs according to His glorious riches in Christ Jesus.

original.text: ὁ δὲ θεός μου πληρώσει πᾶσαν χρείαν ὑμῶν κατὰ ⸂τὸ πλοῦτος⸃ αὐτοῦ ἐν δόξῃ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.

verses.restored: Now to our Divine and Father be glory into the ages of the ages. Amen.

familiar.text: Now unto God and our Father be glory for ever and ever. Amen.

modern.text: To our God and Father be glory forever and ever. Amen. Final Greetings (Ephesians 6:21–24; 2 Timothy 4:19–22)

original.text: τῷ δὲ θεῷ καὶ πατρὶ ἡμῶν ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.

verses.restored: Greet every holy one in Messiah Jesus. The siblings with me greet you.

familiar.text: Salute every saint in Christ Jesus. The brethren which are with me greet you.

modern.text: Greet all the saints in Christ Jesus. The brothers who are with me send you greetings.

original.text: Ἀσπάσασθε πάντα ἅγιον ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ. ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς οἱ σὺν ἐμοὶ ἀδελφοί.

verses.restored: All the holy ones greet you, especially those from Caesar's household.

familiar.text: All the saints salute you, chiefly they that are of Caesar’s household.

modern.text: All the saints send you greetings, especially those from the household of Caesar.

original.text: ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς πάντες οἱ ἅγιοι, μάλιστα δὲ οἱ ἐκ τῆς Καίσαρος οἰκίας.

verses.restored: The grace of the Lord Jesus Messiah be with your spirit.

familiar.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

modern.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.

original.text: ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ ⸂τοῦ πνεύματος⸃ ⸀ὑμῶν.

translation_notes: Philippians 4:13 is contentment-under-conditions language, not triumphalist success formula.
Euodia and Syntyche are honored as women who struggled together with Paul in the good news; the appeal is reconciliation, not diminishment.
